input.text:
Acme services use short-lived bearer tokens for authentication.
- Issuance: a client exchanges its service credential at the token endpoint for an access token scoped to one audience. Tokens last 15 minutes and can't be refreshed, so the client mints a new one when the old one expires.
- Presentation: the token goes in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Services reject requests whose token is missing, expired, or scoped to a different audience.
- Scopes: tokens carry only the scopes the client was granted, and services enforce them per route. There is no ambient authority, so an unscoped token can read nothing.
- Rotation: signing keys rotate weekly. Services trust both the current and previous key, so in-flight tokens survive a rotation.
- Token fields: `sub` (client id), `aud` (single audience), `scope` (space-delimited scopes), `exp` (expiry, 15 minutes after issuance), `kid` (signing key id).
Note: auth.md says the field reference may be stale and points to an optional external schema. I didn't fetch it, so the fields above come from the sandbox doc only.
